transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-06-15 15:10 UTC
- Duration: 46 minutes
- Attendees: Laura Kim (Redwood AE); Marcus Velasquez (Redwood SE); Jin Park (Redwood Solutions); Noah Garcia (CTO, Crescent Financial); Maya Patel (Product); Priya Singh (Head of Security); Ethan Lowe (SRE)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
Redwood and Crescent Financial align on POC goals: protect PII, define retention windows, decide on redaction-before-logging vs log-and-redact, and run a micro-benchmark to validate latency and cost. Action items assigned.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Laura (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, audio good?
[00:07] Noah (Crescent): Yep good here.
[00:09] Laura: Cool. I'll kick off with the objective — we want to scope a short POC to confirm how Redwood handles sensitive payloads for your chat assistant flow. Marcus will walk the technical flow and we'll surface success criteria.
[00:22] Marcus (Redwood SE): Hi all. From our side, the POC typically covers three pillars: ingestion & redaction, storage/retention choices for prompts and responses, and performance benchmarks at representative load. We'll propose a bench plan then run it either in Redwood Dedicated or within your VPC private deployment depending on the security constraints.
[00:40] Maya (Product): A quick note on scope — most sensitive content is account numbers, SSNs, and certain free-text notes clients paste in. We don't want those to be stored in logs in plain text under any circumstance.
[00:52] Priya (Security): Agree. Also we need auditability for redaction decisions; i.e., we want to know what was redacted and why, but without storing the sensitive token.
[01:03] Ethan (SRE): And on SLOs, latency must stay under 350ms p50 for short prompts, and we want to validate at scaled throughput around 50 qps for peak windows.
[01:15] Marcus: Good constraints. Two fundamental approaches: redaction-before-logging (we strip PII on ingress and never persist) or log-then-redact (store raw then run redaction in a walled process). Each has tradeoffs: earlier removes risk but makes debugging harder; latter is easier to debug but increases exposure window and requires hardened storage + access controls.
[01:36] Priya: Our org leans strongly to redaction-before-logging for regulatory reasons; however, we need deterministic redaction and a replay path for debugging (sanitized traces).
[01:47] Laura: Noted. For the POC, we can demonstrate both flows in a controlled environment and compare. We'll also show how Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and batching to control cost while meeting your latency SLO.
[01:58] Maya: How do you actually detect PII? Regex? ML model? We have messy formats.
[02:05] Marcus: Good question. Redwood uses a hybrid detection: high-precision regex rules for structured tokens, augmented with an entity-detection model for contextual PII. For the POC we can tune detection thresholds and surface false positive/negative counts. Note: detection is probabilistic so we log detection confidence levels (but not the raw sensitive value).
[02:25] Noah: On retention: what are the options? We prefer short-lived context store — 24 hours? 7 days? We need a legal hold option too.
[02:31] Jin (Redwood): The platform supports configurable retention windows per route: ephemeral (session-only, purge on session end), short-term (configurable, e.g., 24-72 hours), and long-term (for analytics, with redaction applied). Legal hold can be applied to specific conversation IDs; we can keep metadata only while redacting payloads.
[02:50] Priya: Important — legal hold should not circumvent redaction. If a legal hold is triggered we want the minimal amount retained, and access controls audited.
[03:00] Marcus: We can demonstrate a redaction layer that stores a redaction manifest: which token indices were removed and redaction reason, without storing the original token strings. That satisfies auditability while keeping the sensitive text out.
[03:12] Ethan: How do you prove in the POC that the redaction layer doesn't add steps that break latency SLO?
[03:18] Marcus: We'll include redaction latency in the micro-benchmark. Typical redaction is sub-5ms per request for regex-first approaches; model-based checks add variable cost. The bench will capture p50/p95/p99 with and without redaction, and with batching enabled.
[03:33] Maya: For prompts that include attachments (like base64 blobs), do you have a recommended pattern?
[03:38] Marcus: For large binary attachments we recommend offload to a storage service and pass a sanitized reference. We can detect base64-encoded PII heuristics and flag them for manual review in the POC.
[03:49] Laura: Success criteria for the POC — let's align now. From Redwood's side we propose: (1) redaction removes >99% of sampled PII tokens (precision > 98%), (2) latency delta <= 20% vs baseline without redaction and p50 < 350ms, (3) no raw PII persisted in logs in the redaction-before-logging config, and (4) we can run a micro-benchmark at 50 qps for 15 minutes. Any additions?
[04:16] Priya: Add: audit manifests must include who/when redaction ran and confidence buckets; manifests should be immutable and exportable for compliance review.
[04:26] Noah: And include cost estimate per 1M requests so procurement can evaluate.
[04:32] Marcus: We'll provide cost-per-token estimates for the baseline, batched, and quantized paths. For the bench we will record token counts, GPU utilization, and effective cost-per-1k tokens.
[04:45] Maya: Timeline?
[04:47] Laura: Proposed timeline: security docs and architecture diagram shared by Redwood within 3 business days; customer shares sample payloads and a 48-hour trace within 5 business days; Redwood drafts bench plan in 2 business days after receiving trace; run micro-bench ~1 week from today.
[05:03] Maya: Sounds good. For the micro-bench, do we need production traffic mirrored?
[05:07] Marcus: Mirror is preferred for fidelity, but a sanitized replay is fine — we just need realistic sequence lengths and token distributions. If you can share a 48-hour trace we can synthesize load.
[05:18] Ethan: Any concerns about encryption keys? We use KMS and HSM for some flows.
[05:22] Jin: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for Private deployments. For Hosted we offer encryption at rest with our KMS and optional customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private. We'll include key management options in the security packet.
[05:36] Priya: We also need to confirm RBAC for audit log access — only 2 people from Crescent should be able to request unredacted audit reports (if allowed at all).
[05:45] Laura: Understood. For POC we'll show demo RBAC flows and how manifests are protected behind SSO + role checks.
[05:53] Marcus: One more technical nuance — KV cache and prefix caching: caching can increase throughput and reduce cost but can also leak data if not keyed correctly. For the POC we'll validate cache keys are derived safely and show options for cache partitioning per-tenant or per-route.
[06:08] Noah: Ok that was helpful. Can you outline what you'll send after this call?
[06:12] Laura: Sure — immediate deliverables: security packet (SOC2/ISO summary, architecture diagram, KMS options), proposed bench plan and scripts, and a short redaction demo video. We'll also attach a template for sample payload extraction to make it easy for your team.
[06:26] Maya: We'll aim to get sample payloads and the 48h trace by Friday.
[06:29] Laura: Great. Anything else?
[06:31] Priya: One last ask — include a failure-mode doc: what happens if redaction fails or confidence is low, and how fallbacks are handled.
[06:39] Marcus: We'll include failure-mode flows: reject/hold, mask-only, escalate to manual review depending on policy.
[06:46] Laura: Perfect. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with the packet and calendar invite for the bench run.
[06:52] Noah: Thanks all.
[06:54] Maya: Thanks.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: there's occasional overlap and a few proper nouns may be mistranscribed (e.g., internal service names). Some timestamps approximate speaker turns rather than exact seconds.
